golden_inclusion: Enhanced arterial phase CT images of the neck
Single or multiple enlarged lymph nodes with shortest diameter > 1cm on CT
Pathology confirmed by surgery, biopsy, or clinical follow-up
agent_inclusion: Patients with cervical lymph node imaging studies
Studies showing enlarged cervical lymph nodes
Cross-sectional imaging modalities (CT, MRI, ultrasound)
Adults (age ≥ 18 years)
golden_exclusion: CT images with artefacts affecting observation/measurement
agent_exclusion: Pediatric patients (age < 18 years)
Studies without visible cervical lymph nodes
Non-cross-sectional imaging (e.g., plain films)
Studies with significant artifacts affecting lymph node assessment
Patients with known head and neck malignancies (to focus on benign/unknown etiology)
Post-treatment or post-surgical cases

golden_inclusion: Histopathological confirmation of malignant rectal tumors with no prior antitumor treatment
Performance of contrast-enhanced transrectal ultrasound (CETRUS) stored in standardized format
Completion of contrast-enhanced CT of chest/abdomen/pelvis and liver ultrasound
No previous history of other malignancies
agent_inclusion: Rectal cancer patients
Contrast-enhanced transrectal ultrasound imaging
Patients with documented distant metastasis status
No previous local or systemic treatment for rectal cancer
Images with sufficient technical quality for radiomics analysis
agent_exclusion: Non-rectal cancer diagnoses
Non-contrast ultrasound studies
Patients with incomplete metastasis status documentation
Previous rectal cancer treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery)
Images with significant artifacts affecting analysis
Post-treatment surveillance imaging

golden_inclusion: Complete surgical resection and pathologically confirmed invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC)
Pathology reports containing complete percentages of each High-Grade Pattern (HGP)
Chest CT scans performed 2 weeks prior to surgery with DICOM files available
agent_inclusion: Pathologically confirmed stage IA lung adenocarcinoma
CT scans performed prior to surgical resection
Visible pulmonary nodule(s) consistent with adenocarcinoma
Slice thickness ≤ 1.5mm for adequate radiomic feature extraction
Non-contrast or contrast-enhanced CT scans (portal venous phase if enhanced)
Patients age 18 years or older
golden_exclusion: Variant adenocarcinoma (mucinous, colloid, etc.) or mixed lung carcinoma
Poor image quality due to severe respiratory artefacts
Preoperative history of radiotherapy and chemotherapy
agent_exclusion: Previous lung cancer treatment (chemotherapy, radiation, surgery)
Significant motion artifacts affecting nodule evaluation
Nodule size < 6mm or > 30mm (to exclude ground-glass opacities and large tumors)
Presence of multiple primary lung cancers
Severe emphysema or interstitial lung disease affecting image interpretation
Metastatic disease to lungs from other primary sites

golden_inclusion: Ultrasound diagnosis of breast Non-Mass Lesions (NML)
Breast density confirmed by ultrasound or mammography
Complete clinical data and definite pathological results via biopsy or resection
agent_inclusion: Female patients with dense breast tissue (BI-RADS density categories C or D)
Non-mass lesions on breast ultrasound
Patients with confirmed benign or malignant diagnosis (biopsy-proven)
Complete ultrasound imaging available including radiomic feature extraction capability
golden_exclusion: Preoperative history of neoadjuvant chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or endocrine therapy
Poor ultrasonic image quality, artifacts, or noise
Lesions cannot be measured on ultrasound images
agent_exclusion: Male patients
Patients with breast implants or previous breast surgery
Mass lesions (focal masses with defined borders)
Insufficient image quality for radiomic analysis
Patients without definitive pathological diagnosis
Non-dense breast tissue (BI-RADS A or B density)

golden_inclusion: Histologically confirmed staged I-III invasive breast cancer
Treated with surgery and SLNB or axillary lymph node dissection (ALND)
agent_inclusion: Female patients
Diagnosed with breast cancer
Ultrasound examinations of breast and axilla
Examinations performed for lymph node assessment
Clinical or pathological documentation available
Age 18 years or older
golden_exclusion: Lost to follow-up or incomplete clinicopathological data
agent_exclusion: Male patients
No breast cancer diagnosis
Ultrasound studies without axillary assessment
Prior axillary surgery or intervention
Insufficient clinical documentation
Contrast-enhanced ultrasound studies
Studies with significant artifacts impairing interpretation
